sumInsured: Annual Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule / Customer Information Sheet (not provided in excerpt)

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: “The reset amount can only be used for all future claims within the same policy year, not related to the illness/ disease/ injury for which a claim has been paid in that policy year for the same person.”
good.explanation: The sum insured resets within the same policy year but only for new illnesses or injuries, not for repeated claims on the same condition. This means you get extra coverage for different health issues during the year but not for the same illness.

good.name: No Claim Bonus
good.quote: “At the time of renewal of this Policy, We will provide a Loyalty Bonus of 10% of annual sum insured of immediately preceding policy year subject to a maximum of 100% of the annual sum insured”
good.explanation: You receive a 10% increase in sum insured each claim-free year, up to double the original amount. This rewards you by increasing your coverage on renewal for staying claim-free.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “We will cover the Medical Expenses incurred in respect of Your Domiciliary Hospitalization during the Policy Period… The Domiciliary Hospitalization continues for at least 3 consecutive days…”
good.explanation: Home-based treatment is covered if it lasts at least 3 consecutive days and meets medical criteria. This helps cover treatment costs without hospital admission when medically necessary.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “In consideration of the payment of additional premium to Us, We will cover the expenses incurred on air ambulance services…”
good.explanation: Air ambulance coverage is available if you pay an extra premium. This provides emergency air transport but only if you opt for this add-on.

good.name: OPD Cover
good.quote: “In consideration of the payment of additional premium… We will cover you for the Medical Expenses incurred by You in outpatient.”
good.reference: Section C.14 Out Patient Treatment Cover
good.explanation: Outpatient expenses like consultations and diagnostics can be covered if you buy this add-on. Coverage limits depend on your policy schedule.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “Room rent capping shall be applicable to room rent of a hospital room, ICU/ICCU and will be specified in policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet against the benefit.”
bad.explanation: Room rent is capped as per the policy schedule rather than covering any room at actual cost. This can increase your out-of-pocket expenses if you choose a higher room category.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: “If the insured chooses a higher room category than the category that is eligible as per terms and conditions of the policy then the insured person shall bear the rateable proportion of the total associated medical expenses.”
bad.reference: Section A.1 Hospitalization Expenses (Inpatient Treatment) + Definitions (Associated Medical Expenses)
bad.explanation: Choosing a room category above your eligible limit triggers proportionate deductions on medical bills. This reduces claim payouts and increases your expenses.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Below are the non-payable items applicable in the policy… 56 GLOVES… 60 MASK…”
bad.reference: Part III (ii) 10 Non Payables (List of Non Payable Items)
bad.explanation: Common consumables like gloves and masks are excluded from coverage and must be paid out-of-pocket unless you buy an optional add-on. This can add to your hospital expenses.

bad.name: Pre/Post Hospitalization
bad.quote: “Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses… for a period… as specified against this benefit in the policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet… Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses… as specified against this benefit in the policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet”
bad.reference: Section A.3 Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses
bad.explanation: The number of days covered before and after hospitalization is not stated and depends on the schedule. Without clear limits, coverage may be minimal or absent.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “If opted customer will pay the co -pay as per Zone explained below… Zone 1 Nil Nil Nil; Zone 2 10% Nil Nil; Zone 3 15% 5% Nil”
bad.explanation: The policy includes co-pay options based on geographic zones, requiring you to pay a percentage of claims if you opt in. Any co-pay clause means higher out-of-pocket costs and is considered a disadvantage.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “In case You have opted for a voluntary co-payment, you will be liable to pay the % of admissible claim amount for each and every claim as specified in the policy schedule.”
bad.explanation: Voluntary co-pay means you pay a portion of each claim to reduce premiums. Even if optional, co-pay clauses increase your expenses and are considered negative.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “Claims… shall be subject to… Co-payment (if any) for the Benefit claimed as specified in the Policy Schedule/Certificate”
bad.reference: Section d) WHAT WE WILL PAY (Scope of Cover)
bad.explanation: The policy mentions co-payment may apply as per the schedule but does not clarify if it is mandatory or zero by default. This requires checking the schedule to confirm.

unclear.name: PED Waiting Period
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)… shall be excluded until the expiry of specified months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
unclear.explanation: The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is not specified here and depends on the policy schedule. Without this info, the waiting period cannot be classified.

unclear.name: Specific Illness Waiting
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of specified months of continuous coverage…”
unclear.reference: Exclusions 3.2 Code-Excl02: Specified disease/procedure waiting period
unclear.explanation: Waiting period for specific illnesses or procedures is schedule-based and not stated here. The exact duration needs to be confirmed from the schedule.

unclear.name: Initial Waiting Period
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within specified days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident…”
unclear.explanation: The initial waiting period duration is not specified and depends on the policy schedule. This needs confirmation to determine if it meets market standards.
